messages:
maria-plat: Heads-up — we need a clear policy for smart routing + fallback for Private (VPC/on-prem) customers who deny egress. Customer asked that we never cross regions or hit public internet. How do we handle model variant fallbacks when primary isn't available?
aj-router: Short answer: prefer same-region variants, then same-region smaller/quantized variants. Cross-region fallback must be opt-in at the control-plane level.
leo-sec: Agree. For customers with egress=deny we cannot reach external checkpoints or cross-region endpoints. That constraint must be enforced by the router before any connection attempts.
sara-console: UX ask: console needs a per-customer summary: allowed_regions, egress_policy, last_fallback_event (time+reason). Ops and sales want to view fallback frequency during rollouts.
aj-router: Implementation sketch: router consults customer_metadata from control plane: {allowed_regions:[], egress_policy: "deny|restricted|open", tier: "enterprise|standard|free"}. Routing algorithm: 1) pick candidate nodes in request_region ∩ allowed_regions, 2) prefer same model family and quantized variant, 3) if none and cross-region allowed -> try region order; else fail with clear error with code ROUTE_NO_LOCAL_VARIANT.
leo-sec: Also: audit log entry on any attempted cross-region fallback. We need to record customer_consent_id for legal. Telemetry event name: routing.fallback.record with tags: customer_id, from_region, attempted_region, model_variant, reason.
maria-plat: What about tier-based relaxations? For small-tier customers we sometimes allow cross-region fallback to preserve availability. Is that acceptable?
aj-router: Yes but must be explicit: customer_metadata.allow_cross_region_fallback: boolean. Default: false for Private installs. For hosted/dedicated default true for standard tiers.
sara-console: For rollouts UX: add checkbox in canary rollout flow: "Allow cross-region fallback for this customer" + a notice about egress/legal. Also show expected SLA delta and an estimated cost delta.
aj-router: Example routing config (yaml):
```
routing_policy:
  - match:
      region: eu-west-1
      customer_tier: enterprise
    prefer: same_region
    fallback:
      - same_region:
          variants: [redwood/gpt-large-q4_0, redwood/gpt-medium-q4_0]
      - cross_region_allowed: false
      - error_on_no_variant: true
```
leo-sec: Router must enforce egress ACLs at two checkpoints: 1) pre-route check (deny if no allowed_region), 2) before opening any external connection (double-check). If either fails, return 403-like error to caller and emit telemetry.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary routing-service v2.8 -> eu-west-1 started at 2024-12-10T09:12:03Z
maria-plat: Edge-case: on-prem air-gapped customers often expect control plane to never be in the data path. We still need control-plane-originated metadata sync, but we must support local-only routing configs that are fully editable in the private control plane.
aj-router: Right — support two modes: managed-control-plane and self-hosted-control-plane. In self-hosted mode router reads local_policy store and refuses any remote-control-plane overrides.
sara-console: UI needs to surface mode and block toggles when in self-hosted mode. Also allow admins to simulate fallback scenarios (simulate fallback button) and export CSV for audits.
leo-sec: Telemetry/data retention: fallback events are sensitive. For Private customers enable opt-in telemetry export; default keep only counts+hashes (no PII). Store full logs only if customer opts in and signs DPA.
maria-plat: One more: error surface. If we deny cross-region fallback, the API response should include structured reason so apps can show user-friendly message and optionally fallback client-side. Suggested body: {error: "ROUTE_NO_LOCAL_VARIANT", reason: "no compatible model variant in allowed regions", suggested_action: "set allow_cross_region_fallback in console or pick smaller model variant"}.
aj-router: Agree. We'll also emit metrics: routing.fallback.attempts, routing.fallback.allowed_by_policy, routing.fallback.blocked_by_egress. Those should be labeled by customer_tier and region.
sara-console: I'll mock a dashboard panel: "Fallbacks by customer" + timeline + per-rollout filter. Also add an alert threshold for >1% fallback rate during canary.
leo-sec: Dev task: add enforcement unit tests and a security e2e where control-plane is unreachable and router must still honor stored local policy.
maria-plat: Ok action items: @aj-router draft RFC for router policy changes + YAML schema and runtime checks (due EOW). @sara-console wireframe for fallback history and per-customer controls (due next Wed). @leo-sec draft telemetry/data-retention options and audit log spec (due EOW). I'll coordinate with legal on consent wording.
aj-router: ack. I'll include example gRPC error codes and sample client responses.
devops-bot: routing-service v2.8 canary health: ok (3/3 nodes healthy).
maria-plat: thanks — keeping this thread for traceability. If anyone changes control-plane schema ping here. :thumbsup:
